title: Folong (Hako Diam) sauté
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Fresh folong leaves blanched in natron water, then added to a fried base of onion, smoked fish, tomato and spices for 10–15 minutes; may be made with meat, fish or plain.
longDesc: p. 62 of the October 2023 recipe book. Fresh folong leaves are blanched in natron water, then added to the fried base for 10–15 minutes. The page says the dish can be made with meat, smoked or fresh fish, or plain. No quantities are printed.
ingredients: Fresh folong leaves — quantity not printed
Oil, onion, garlic, tomato, bell pepper, leeks, parsley, celery, white pepper, ginger, salt, chilli — quantities not printed
steps: Blanch the leaves in natron water.
Fry the onion; add the fish, tomato and seasonings.
Add the leaves and cook 10–15 minutes.
chefTips: Printed variants: meat, smoked or fresh fish, or plain.
No doneness cue is printed beyond the times.
healthBenefits: A leafy green sauté with fish.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe. The page uses ‘hako diam’ as a second name.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Folong (hako diam) sauté’ (p. 62).
